member: Dr. Amara Okafor — Soft Skin Mechanics
message:
My soft skin proposal builds directly on two proven fingertip skins. The GelSight: High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors for Estimating Geometry and Force (E2) shows a clear silicone elastomer with Shore A values between 5 and 20 and neo-Hookean coefficient mu of 0.145 megapascal (MPa) in a domed sheet under 2.5 millimetre (mm) thick, and the SynTouch - BioTac (E3) shows a rigid core surrounded by an elastic liquid-filled skin giving human-fingertip compliance, so I propose a molded 20 mm diameter by 22 mm long silicone dome with 1.5 mm skin over gel on a rigid core as drawn in the fingertip section sketch (E15), using purchasable silicones of the Dragon Skin 30 vs. Ecoflex 5 type (E11), where 1 millinewton (mN) spreads to 0.47 mm diameter at 5.78 kilopascal (kPa) mean pressure in the Hertz spot size (E14) made with the soft-touch sizing skill (E1), which is a grain of sand on an adult fingertip at about one-twentieth of an atmosphere and therefore a gentle but transducible touch.

Fingerprint ridges are needed for slip because ridges select and amplify vibration for detection. The The role of fingerprints in the coding of tactile information probed with a biomimetic sensor (E5) shows a ridged biomimetic surface makes vibration spectra dominated by scanning speed over interridge distance and tuned into the Pacinian receptor band, so I propose molded 0.4 mm pitch by 0.1 mm high ridges that put normal finger slip speeds into hundreds of hertz where Prof. Kenji Tanaka, Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Reid can detect them.

Skin stiffness and bonding must preserve that light-touch pressure through to transduction. The Convert Durometer to Young's Modulus (E4) gives about 0.667 MPa for Shore A 10 silicone, soft enough for the 1 mN spot above yet moldable and durable, and the edge must be primer-bonded and clamped to a nail-backed core so grip load goes into the finger while the soft stack above transduction stays under 2.5 mm thick per the GelSight: High-Resolution Robot Tactile Sensors for Estimating Geometry and Force (E2).

Not ready, because transduction, localization and transmission choices from Prof. Kenji Tanaka, Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Reid are still missing to close the 1 mN signal path.
